title: Long UUP — Dollar Strength as September Hike Probability Crosses 60% For the First Time
entry: $28.20–28.55 zone (DXY ~100.90; UUP near 52-week high $28.56; enter on any intraday pullback toward $28.20; do not chase a gap above $28.55 as that puts the position immediately at technical resistance with a narrow stop buffer).
stop_loss: $27.75 daily close (~2.3% below $28.39 reference) — at $27.75, DXY has broken sustainably below 99.50, which implies either (1) an Iran-US ceasefire removes the oil-driven inflation narrative and September hike probability collapses below 50%, or (2) the FOMC July 28–29 statement delivers an unexpectedly dovish pivot that causes the dollar to reprice lower regardless of the oil backdrop. Two consecutive closes below $27.75 confirm the thesis is broken; exit the position fully without averaging down.
targets: $28.90 — DXY breaks 102; September hike probability holds 65%+ through the FOMC July 28–29 statement; WTI closes the week above $85; first-target DXY 102 close triggers 40% take-profit; EUR/USD breaking 1.09 is the confirming signal
$29.40 — FOMC July 28–29 statement explicitly acknowledges September as 'likely'; DXY breaks 103; September hike probability at 80%+; EUR/USD below 1.07; USD/JPY above 155; cover 40%
$30.00 — September rate hike confirmed by August FOMC prep or Jackson Hole communication; DXY tests 105; August CPI above 3.5% removes ambiguity from Fed's September decision; hold final 20%
catalyst: September 2026 FOMC rate hike probability crossed 60% for the first time in the current cycle on July 22, 2026 — driven by WTI surging to $87.56 overnight after Secretary Rubio declared Iran 'not serious' about peace talks. At 69% September hike probability, five of seven formal regime indicators are now breached. The FOMC meets July 28–29 with a hawkish oil-inflation backdrop; the statement's characterization of September language is the clearing event. DXY at ~100.90 reflects two competing forces (hawkish rate differential positive vs. oil inflation terms-of-trade negative) that historically resolve in favor of rate-differential dollar strength when September hike probability crosses 60%.
thesis:
UUP provides clean DXY exposure at a moment when the dollar faces two competing forces that historically favor net strength: a hawkish Fed repricing through the rate-differential channel, and a safe-haven bid through the flight-to-quality channel during geopolitical stress. Both forces are simultaneously active on July 22. The rate-differential effect is the primary driver: above 60% September hike probability, the dollar's 2-year yield pickup vs. EUR, JPY, and GBP expands materially, attracting capital flows to USD-denominated assets. The safe-haven effect adds a second bid layer as WTI at $87.56 depresses EUR and JPY (both oil importers facing deteriorating terms of trade) relative to USD (the US is energy-independent through Permian production). UUP captures the net dollar strength through its DXY-weighted basket: EUR 57.6%, JPY 13.6%, GBP 11.9%, CAD 9.1%, SEK 4.2%, CHF 3.6%.

The September hike probability crossing 60% is specifically significant because it marks the first time markets have formally priced a September rate hike above the decision threshold. Below 60%, the Fed is in the 'watching and waiting' mode — a stance that is dollar-neutral as markets expect rate stability. Above 60%, the market begins to model both the rate hike itself (25bps September) and the signaling implications for December and beyond (if September hikes, does December follow?). This shifts the expected rate path for USD against all major currencies, widening rate differentials that capital flows respond to with a 2–3 week lead time. The FOMC July 28–29 meeting is the clearing event: if the statement contains language such as 'additional firming may be warranted' or 'remain committed to returning inflation to 2%,' the September hike probability will move above 75% and the dollar should follow.

Oil at $87.56 WTI / $94.20 Brent adds an asymmetric positive for the dollar that runs through the EUR/JPY weakness channel. Europe and Japan import approximately 90% of their crude oil; at Brent $94.20, their trade deficits widen mechanically. EUR/USD historically declines 0.5–1.0% per each $5 increment above Brent $80 as the current-account transmission operates. This is consistent with the morning briefing's DXY read of 'mild risk-off bid balanced by oil-driven inflation concerns' — the balance is not exactly neutral; the rate differential and oil-importer weakness effects both push dollar up against the rate-differential benefit.

This is the thinnest risk/reward trade in today's slate, which is why position sizing is 2% — the smallest allowed. UUP is already near its 52-week high ($28.56), limiting the upside from resistance and requiring a genuine macro regime break (the FOMC statement) rather than just an extension of current momentum. The trade's value is as a macro hedge and portfolio completer: the existing slate is long equities and long oil, while UUP provides a dollar-long hedge that benefits when the rate hawkishness becomes so severe that equity longs are at risk.
bull_case: FOMC July 28–29 statement explicitly flags September as 'likely' for the first time; August CPI prints 3.5%+ forcing clarity on the September decision; EUR/USD breaks 1.08; DXY tests 103–105; UUP to $29.40–30.00. The bull case requires the FOMC not to explicitly dismiss September, which is increasingly difficult when September hike probability is already at 69%.
bear_case: GOOGL/TSLA double beat tonight triggers risk-on; September hike probability retreats from 69% to 50% as bond markets price earnings relief overriding oil; Iran back-channel contacts emerge over the weekend (Rubio/Araghchi Oman meeting reported); WTI reverses from $87.56 toward $80 on the diplomatic news; DXY back to 99–100; UUP to $27.75 stop triggered.
invalidation: $27.75 UUP daily close; OR Iran-US ceasefire formally announced with Hormuz re-opening (WTI below $79 removes oil-inflation dollar support); OR September hike probability falls below 40% on two consecutive sessions; OR DXY closes below 99.00 for two consecutive sessions; OR FOMC July 28–29 statement is explicitly dovish (rates appropriate, inflation trending down) that causes September hike probability to collapse below 35%.
